findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11(A) Demonstration. The operators present were unaware of many of the nuances associated with safe food handling. In particular, storage order, hand washing, sanitizing, and cleaning seemed to be lacking. The facility will have several opportunities to correct the violations observed during today’s inspection. The follow-up with this violation will occur in over a month to ensure discussions and educations resulting from today are being properly applied to the daily operations. It would be of benefit to have all staff participate in the certified food managers course. The knowledge gained during that course can only help with safe food handling. 


Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (A) Complying with this Code by having no violations of PRIORITY ITEMS during the current inspection. [PF]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: The signed employee health reporting agreement forms for each employee were not available during the inspection. The operator informed the inspector that the owner of the facility was not available to provide the signed copies. The inspector also gave blank copies to the operator. Ensure all employees sign and maintain employee health reporting agreement forms on-site. The inspector will follow up on 04/06/2026 to verify compliance.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [PF]

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use.
findings.citation_text:
2-401.11(B) Eating, Drinking, or Using TOBACCO PRODUCTS. Personal products are being stored throughout the kitchen (see violation #56) but there is a half-used drinking bottle of water on the right side of the preparation cooler. Cease storing personal products in various areas throughout the kitchen (inclusive of clothing and other sundries). See that personal beverages are being stored on the shelf adjacent to the hand sink so that hands may be properly washed after taking a drink. 

An employee may drink from a closed container with a lid and a straw and then return to work. Any other cup, can, or bottle needs to be followed with a hand washing occasion. 
Discussed storage of personal foods. The space should be re-evaluated to account for the minimal space and the volume of personal items present. Use a cup with a lid and straw or store the bottle by the hand sink. 

(B) A FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from a closed BEVERAGE container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of: (1) The EMPLOYEE'S hands; (2) The container; and (3) Exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT - 2-301.14 When to Wash. Observed an employee donning gloves without a proper hand washing occasion. The operator was previously in the walk-in cooler and moving boxes of items. Halted the behavior of donning gloves and requested the staff member wash hands. Proper hand washing technique was observed. 
In addition, the operators were later observed changing gloves and moving items at the request of inspectors without washing hands. The scene became hectic as inspectors were requesting information while food was being prepared, but hand washing opportunities should not be missed. 

FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [C]

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. Portion cups are being used as scoops in the seasoning containers by the service counter. See that proper scoops with a handle are available for use. Store the scoop so the handle is presented out of the food. Avoid allowing hands to touch the product. 
Follow-up is occurring on 4/6/26 due to the availability of the inspector. 


(B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. Observed a grocery bag being used to hold seasonings. Grocery bags are not approved for direct food contact and should not be used as a storage device. Cease storing spices in grocery sacks. 
(A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings. [C]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. Observed multiple instances of improper storage. The walk-in cooler has chicken over fish. Fish over butter. Chicken over beef. And Chicken over cut green peppers. The walk-in cooler is small for the amount of food present. See that storage is corrected to allow for proper storage: washed and cut produce, over unwashed produce, over fish, beef/pork, chicken, and then personal foods on the bottom. Change storage of foods to prevent the potential for cross-contamination. 


 (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. Boxes of food are observed being stored on the floor of the walk-in freezer. Operator moved the foods during the inspection. Again, storage and organization must be maintained to keep this small space working properly. 


(A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(D) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. There was not a sanitizing bucket available to store in-use wiping cloths. A bucket was created during the inspection and test strips were available to check the concentration of the product. See that sani-buckets are available for the operators to store their wet wiping cloths within the solution between uses. 

 A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (D) If another solution of a chemical specified under (A) - (C) of this section is used, the PERMIT HOLDER shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY that the solution achieves SANITIZATION and the use of the solution shall be APPROVED. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. The interior of the microwave is observed soiled with food from repeated use. Clean the interior of the microwave. 

(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [PF]

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. A half dozen baked potatoes were observed in a container atop the microwave by the fryers. A potato was probed at 76F. The potato that was probed was discarded. The product is going to be held using TIME AS CONTROL. Discussed with operator the need to identify the time the food was created and then control for FOUR HOURS. The baked potatoes were created at 11am, so they would need to be discarded by 3pm. 

And then, 3:30pm arrived and inspectors returned to the kitchen to see that the potatoes were discarded. The inspectors observed that the potatoes had been discarded by the operator. A discussion was again held with the operators that upgrading to a Class I permit would allow for foods to be cooled and reheated. The ideal handling for the baked potatoes are to cook several, cool, and then store in the preparation cooler. That would eliminate the counter storage. 

The four hours rule is not the best option for a facility that cannot control the time. 


 (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. Observed two boxes of chicken wings stored on a counter to the right as you enter the kitchen. Wings were present during the inspection without being addressed. The operators were busy with a steady lunch rush. When questioned, the operators indicated the foods were brought from another store two hours prior. The chicken wings were probed at 56F. The boxes were quickly moved into the walk-in cooler for proper cold holding. Discussed NOT storing foods on the counter for future handling during busy periods. Move foods out of temperature control as they are going to be handled. 

(A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. No foods within the facility are noted to have date marking present. There were multiple cooked foods in the walk-in cooler and bulk foods in the preparation cooler that could have potentially carried a date mark. See that foods held longer than 24 hours are dated with the date foods are opened. This includes the cooked gyro meat, sausages and hot dogs, and any prepared foods. 
Raw proteins do NOT need a date marking. 

(A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. The available bleach is not approved for food contact surfaces. Discussed using a product that is USEPA registered. Provide a proper chemical for sanitizing. Operator indicated that the kitchen should have one bleach for sanitizing and one for floors, walls, and ceilings. This was not observed. Only one type of bleach was present and it did not meet the requirements. 

Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), or (B) Meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020 Pesticide Chemicals Not Requiring a Tolerance or Exemption from Tolerance-Nonfood determinations. [P]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: No ambient thermometers were observed in the walk-in cooler and 2 door cooler by the window. The operator was informed and instructed to provide internal thermometers in each of the coolers to allow for proper temperature monitoring, especially in the event of equipment failure. Ensure ambient thermometers are placed in the warmest part of each cooler to accurately monitor internal temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. The dry storage shelving is full of bulk containers of white powders and other seasonings without common name labeling. Label white powders and clear liquids with common name.

The cheese cake in the dessert cooler is not labeled. Provide ingredient labeling to be available for the general public should they ask for contents. 

Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Food Storage. Observed several uncovered containers of food in the walk-in cooler contained amongst soiled shelving. Clean the shelving of the walk-in cooler and see that foods are properly covered while in storage.  

(A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14(D) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. No sani-bucket was available for wiping cloth storage. Wiping cloths are observed on counters around the kitchen. Sani-bucket was created during the inspection and wiping cloths were told to be stored within the bucket. 

 (D) Dry wiping cloths and the chemical sanitizing solutions specified in Subparagraph (B)(1) of this section in which wet wiping cloths are held between uses shall be free of FOOD debris and visible soil. [C]

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. A single-service tin container is observed stored on the bottom shelf of the dry storage rack holding seasonings and spills from the upper shelving. The single-service pan is not inverted and thus is open to storage of all spilled foods. Discard this container. 

(C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Ice accumulation was observed on the plumbing line in the walk-in freezer. The operator was instructed to ensure the plumbing line is cleaned to sight and touch and kept free of ice buildup.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The following non-food contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. The fan covers in the walk-in cooler and walk-in freezer were observed to have dust accumulation. 
2. The 2-door cooler by window was observed to have soil accumulation
3. SECOND REPEAT - The hood above the fryer and the side of the fryer were observed to have soil and grease accumulation.

The inspector instructed the operator to ensure the non-food contact surfaces mentioned above are cleaned to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following areas in the facility were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. The ceiling tiles and air return above the drink shelf were observed to have dust accumulation.
2. The floor area beneath the storage table by the water heater was observed to have grease and soil accumulation.
3. Ice buildup was observed on the floor in the walk-in freezer.
4. Food debris was observed on the floor area between the water heater by the mop sink and the storage table.
5. The floor drain was observed to be soiled.
6. The plumbing at the triple sink was observed to be soiled.
7. The wall at the triple was observed to have soil accumulation.
8. The ceiling tiles and air return above the storage table by the water heater were observed to have dust accumulation.

The inspector instructed the operator to ensure these areas are cleaned to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment:
Pants and coats belonging to employees were observed to be stored on the dry storage rack for spices. The operator was instructed to move the pants and coats away from foods items used for customers in order to prevent contamination.

The inspector also observed the employees’ foods were stored with food items used for customers in the walk-in cooler. The inspector instructed the operator to ensure employee foods are stored at the bottom of the cooler, away from foods for customers.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Two employees handling foods were observed to not have food handlers’ certificates. The operator was instructed to ensure all employees handling foods are certified in safe food handling. Ensure all food handlers obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Allergen awareness notice
findings.comment:
The facility has no allergy notice available. Allergen declaration notice was provided during their inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.08(a). Food Allergy awareness. (a) A restaurant shall display a notice indicating to consumers that any information regarding food allergies must be communicated to an employee of the restaurant. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Inspector observed staff members donning gloves without washing their hands. Staff members were educated and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that employees are knowledgeable to wash their hands always before donning gloves.  


When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Inspector observed the accumulation of soil on the hood of the fryer including the accumulation of grease on the side of the fryer. Discussed with PIC. PIC ensured inspector that the relevant cleaning will be done. Ensure that this accumulation of soil and grease are cleaned appropriately. 

Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Food obtained from approved source
findings.comment:
3-201.11: Inspector observed gyro meat cooling in the bottom of the prep cooler at 67F. The facility wants to remain at medium risk for processes. The facility will cook and hold hot only. Gyro meat left at the end of the day will be discarded in the garbage. Ten pounds of gyro meat was discarded in the garbage at the time of inspection. There is an open spot on the hot well to hold cooked meat. 

(A)-(B) FOOD shall be obtained from APPROVED source and not from private home. P

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: Inspector observed that some non food contact areas including storage tables, walls, hood vents have accumulated soil. Clean and maintain the facility in a clean and sanitary manner. 
NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Garbage & refuse properly disposed; facilities maintained
findings.comment:
5-501.115: Inspector observed that a fenced in area originally designed as an enclosure for refuse is in disrepair and has collected unnecessary items including litter. Maintain areas outside of the building clean organized and free of unnecessary items including litter.

A storage area and enclosure for REFUSE, recyclables, or returnables shall be maintained free of unnecessary items, as specified under § 6-501.114, and clean.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: Inspector observed the floor under the storage table holding cleaners is heavily soiled. Clean the area and maintain it free of accumulated soil. 
(A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.113: Maintenance tools are stored in the mop sink in a disorderly fashion. Organize and maintain this area.

Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 
The floor sink under the 3 part sink is heavily soiled. Clean and maintain clean.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

The employees have taken their handler course but do not have possession of their certificates at this time. Provide handler certificates in the Public Health paperwork folder by the next routine inspection.
